title: A Bed, a Chair, a Lamp
story: A Special Room for the Prophet
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
A kind and loving woman saw
the prophet, passing through.
She fed him, then she said, “Let’s build
a cozy room, brand new.”

[Chorus]
Be kind and make some room, my love,
for others, big and small.
The Lord remembers kindness done;
He sees and blesses all.

[Verse 2]
A table and a little chair,
a lamp beside the bed.
Elisha said, “Next year you’ll hold
a baby boy,” he said.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Now close your eyes in your own bed,
your lamp is turned down low.
The Lord who blessed that kindly home
is here and loves you so.

[Chorus]
mood: Homemaking music. A soft, rocking sway under the voice, at the pace of someone tidying a small room and setting a lamp on a table, cozy and content. The chorus warms and widens a little, the way a welcome does. By the last verse the sway slows and lowers, like the lamp being turned down, until the room is dim and safe.
